provider_option_rows.provider_label: Cloudflare DNS + edge certificates + WAF + cache rules
provider_option_rows.dns_summary: One control plane covers proxied DNS, wildcard preview DNS, host-based separation, and fail-closed unknown-host posture.
provider_option_rows.tls_summary: Edge certificates, HSTS, and strict origin TLS fit the stable host inventory without multi-provider drift.
provider_option_rows.waf_summary: Managed WAF, custom rules, and rate limits can stay typed per surface family and callback exception set.
provider_option_rows.cache_summary: Cache Rules cleanly express bypass for session/callback flows and immutable reuse for hashed static assets.
provider_option_rows.preview_summary: Wildcard review domains are easy to isolate without letting preview hosts become provider-trusted callback surfaces.
notes: Chosen as the default unified edge platform because prior cards did not fix an edge provider upstream.
Default does not authorize live mutation; it only freezes the portable policy and inventory set.

provider_option_rows.dns_summary: Capable but split across Route 53, CloudFront, ACM, and AWS WAF instead of one edge control plane.
provider_option_rows.tls_summary: TLS posture is workable, but certificate and DNS ownership split makes host/callback inventory drift easier.
provider_option_rows.waf_summary: WAF and rate limiting are capable, but exception review spans multiple AWS surfaces and policies.
provider_option_rows.cache_summary: CloudFront policies can express the law, but host/path policy review is less unified than the default option.
provider_option_rows.preview_summary: Preview-domain isolation is feasible but less direct than a single wildcard edge platform.
notes: Retained as a credible alternative if platform ownership mandates AWS-native edge.
